question: What was NVIDIA's total revenue in fiscal year 2026?
answer:
NVIDIA's total revenue for fiscal year 2026 (the year ended January 25, 2026) was $215,938 million, or about $215.9 billion.

## What the filing says
- Revenue was $215,938 million in fiscal 2026, up from $130,497 million in fiscal 2025 and $60,922 million in fiscal 2024 [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].
- Growth from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2026 was about 65.5%. My arithmetic: (215,938 − 130,497) ÷ 130,497 ≈ 0.655.
- Data Center was the largest end market at $193,737 million. That is about 89.7% of the total (193,737 ÷ 215,938). Gaming was $16,042 million, Professional Visualization $3,191 million, Automotive $2,349 million, and OEM and Other $619 million [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.79].
- Within Data Center, Compute was $162,361 million and Networking was $31,376 million [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.79].
- By customer headquarters location, the United States was $149,617 million, Taiwan $42,345 million, China (including Hong Kong) $19,677 million, and Other $4,299 million [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.78]. NVIDIA changed to this basis in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and recast prior years to match [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.78].
- Net income, the profit left after all costs and taxes, was $120,067 million [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].

## What this might mean
Revenue grew by about two-thirds in a year, and almost all of it came from Data Center. That means NVIDIA's results depend heavily on that one market. The geographic split follows the customer's headquarters, not necessarily where products end up. The filing estimates that 76% of Data Center revenue from Taiwan-headquartered customers went to end customers in the United States and Europe.

question: How fast did NVIDIA's revenue grow last year?
answer:
NVIDIA's revenue grew 65% in fiscal year 2026 (the year ended January 25, 2026). It rose from $130.5 billion to $215.9 billion. I took "last year" to mean its most recent fiscal year.

## What the filing says
- Revenue was $215,938 million in fiscal 2026, against $130,497 million the year before. The filing calls this "Up 65%" [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.37]. My check: $215,938M − $130,497M = $85,441M, and $85,441M ÷ $130,497M ≈ 65.5% [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.40].
- The Compute & Networking segment grew 67%, from $116,193M to $193,479M. Graphics grew 57%, from $14,304M to $22,459M [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.40].
- Within Compute & Networking, Data Center computing revenue grew 59% on demand for the Blackwell platform. Data Center networking grew 142% [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.40].
- Across all of Data Center, revenue rose 68%. Gaming rose 41%, Professional Visualization 70% and Automotive 39% [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.37].
- Growth was slower than the year before. Fiscal 2025 revenue was up 114%, from $60,922M to $130,497M [NVIDIA FY2025 10-K, p.41].
- Profit did not grow faster than revenue in every respect. Gross margin (the share of revenue left after the direct cost of products) fell from 75.0% to 71.1%. Net income rose 65%, the same as revenue [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.37].

## What this might mean
NVIDIA's sales grew by about two-thirds on top of an already much larger base. That is a slower percentage rate than the prior year, but the dollar increase ($85.4B) was larger than the prior year's ($69.6B). Most of the growth came from Data Center products tied to AI.

question: Does NVIDIA depend on a few big customers?
answer:
Yes. In fiscal 2026 (year ended January 25, 2026), NVIDIA says its revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers. Two direct customers alone made up about 36% of revenue (22% + 14%), up from the prior year.

## What the filing says
- **Company's own wording:** "Our revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers and this trend may continue." [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.41]
- **Fiscal 2026 sales:** One direct customer was 22% of total revenue and another was 14%. Both were primarily in the Compute & Networking segment. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.41]
- **Fiscal 2025:** One direct customer was 12% and two others were 11% each. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.41] In fiscal 2024, one direct customer was 13%. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.41] The FY2025 10-K says no customer reached 10% in fiscal 2023. [NVIDIA FY2025 10-K, p.41]
- **Money owed to NVIDIA:** Three direct customers made up 25%, 18% and 13% of accounts receivable (money customers owe but haven't yet paid) at January 25, 2026. That is 56% combined. A year earlier, two customers made up 17% and 16%. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.67]
- **Who "direct customers" are:** They include distributors, system makers, cloud service providers (CSPs) and AI model makers. Indirect customers buy through them. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.41]

## What this might mean
NVIDIA's sales lean more heavily on a handful of buyers than in the earlier years shown, and those same buyers owe it a large share of its unpaid bills. The filing doesn't name the customers. Some "direct" customers may be intermediaries that resell to others, so the true end-customer picture is less clear.

question: How much cash does NVIDIA have?
answer:
As of January 25, 2026 (the end of NVIDIA's fiscal 2026), NVIDIA had $10.6 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Including marketable securities, it had about $62.6 billion.

## What the filing says
- **Cash and cash equivalents:** $10,605 million at Jan 25, 2026, up from $8,589 million a year earlier. Cash equivalents are very safe, short-term holdings, such as money market funds. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.53]
- **Marketable securities:** $51,951 million, up from $34,621 million. These are investments that can be sold fairly easily, such as U.S. Treasuries and corporate debt. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.53]
- **Combined:** The filing says NVIDIA "had $62.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities." That matches my sum: 10,605 + 51,951 = 62,556 million. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.43]
- **Caveat on the securities:** Marketable securities include $12,886 million of publicly-held equity securities. The filing notes that $10.5 billion of investments are subject to short-term lock-up restrictions on selling. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.65]
- **Cash generation:** Operating activities produced $102,718 million of cash in fiscal 2026. Share repurchases used $40,086 million. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.55]
- **Debt:** Debt was $8,468 million, of which $999 million is due within a year. No commercial paper was outstanding. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.70]

## What this might mean
"Cash" can mean the narrow figure ($10.6 billion) or the broader pool ($62.6 billion). The company itself uses the broader figure when it discusses liquidity. The broader pool is larger than the debt shown. Part of it is equity stakes that may not be quickly sellable, so it is not all equally easy to spend.

- AMD's fiscal year runs 52 or 53 weeks and ends on the last Saturday in December. Fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023 each had 52 weeks, so the three years are comparable in length. [Advanced Micro Devices FY2025 10-K, p.81]

question: Is AMD making money, and is it getting better?
answer:
Yes. AMD was profitable in fiscal 2025 (the year ended December 27, 2025), and revenue, operating profit and net income all rose from the two prior years shown.

## What the filing says
- **Revenue:** Net revenue was $34.6 billion in 2025, up 34% from $25.8 billion in 2024 [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.63]. The 2023 figure was $22.7 billion [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- **Profit:** Net income was $4,335 million in 2025, against $1,641 million in 2024 and $854 million in 2023. Diluted earnings per share were $2.65, $1.00 and $0.53 [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- **Net income details:** The 2025 figure includes a $103 million income tax benefit and $66 million from discontinued operations (a business no longer part of AMD) [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- **Operating income** (profit from running the business, before interest and taxes) was $3,694 million in 2025, $1,900 million in 2024 and $401 million in 2023 [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.74]. By my arithmetic, that is about 10.7% of revenue in 2025 (3,694 ÷ 34,639), 7.4% in 2024 and 1.8% in 2023.
- **Gross margin** (the share of revenue left after the direct cost of making products) was 50% in 2025, up from 49% in 2024. That includes about $440 million of inventory charges tied to U.S. export controls on one AI chip, the MI308 [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.63].
- **Where growth came from:** Data Center revenue rose 32% to $16.6 billion. Client and Gaming rose 51% to $14.6 billion. Embedded fell 3% to $3.5 billion [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.63, p.68]. Data Center operating income barely moved, at $3,603 million versus $3,482 million [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.68].
- **Cash:** Cash and short-term investments were $10.6 billion, up from $5.1 billion a year earlier [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.63].

## What this might mean
AMD looks clearly profitable, and the trend over the three years shown is upward. Profit has grown faster than sales, so more of each revenue dollar is turning into profit. Data Center's profit was nearly flat despite higher sales, and Embedded shrank. Some of the 2025 net income came from a tax benefit and discontinued operations, so operating income is the cleaner measure of the core business.

question: How much of AMD's revenue came from data centers in 2025, and how fast did it grow?
answer:

## What the filing says
- Data Center net revenue was $16,635 million in 2025, against $12,579 million in 2024. AMD reports this as a 32% increase. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.68]
- Total company net revenue was $34,639 million, up 34%. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.63]

[AMD FY2025 10-K, p.68]

## What this might mean
Data Center is AMD's largest segment, at roughly half of sales. Client and Gaming grew faster in 2025, which is why Data Center's share of revenue slipped slightly. Data Center profit rose far less than its revenue, and the filing links that to higher costs and the export-control charge.

question: What are the biggest risks for AMD?
answer:
AMD's FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended December 27, 2025) lists competition, a cyclical industry, reliance on outside chip manufacturers, and U.S. export controls as its main risks. The company doesn't rank them, so this order is my own judgement. The filing calls them risks that "could" hurt results, not predictions.

## What the filing says
- **Competition:** The markets are "highly competitive and rapidly evolving." AMD says Intel uses its position to price aggressively and target AMD's customers and channel partners with special incentives. It says Nvidia uses its data-center GPU position, financial resources and software ecosystem to influence customers. It also names Arm-based designs and customers building their own AI chips as threats. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.28]
- **Cyclical demand, customers and timing:** The summary lists a "highly cyclical" semiconductor industry with "severe downturns." It also lists dependence on launching products on time and the point that "the loss of a significant customer may have a material adverse effect." [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.25]
- **Reliance on manufacturers:** AMD relies on third-party foundries (outside factories that make its chips). If TSMC can't make enough 7 nm-or-smaller wafers, AMD says this "could have a material adverse effect." Lower manufacturing yields could raise unit costs and hurt gross margin. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.35, p.38]
- **Export controls, especially China:** U.S. rules restrict shipping certain Instinct AI chips and Versal FPGAs to China without a license. AMD says tighter controls could limit its ability to meet demand abroad. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.45, p.46]
- **A realized example:** In Q2 2025, AMD recorded about $800 million of inventory and related charges on MI308 data-center GPUs after new export restrictions. It later got some licenses and reversed about $360 million in Q4. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.64] Net charges in cost of sales were about $440 million. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.88]

## What this might mean
AMD's risks are mostly outside its control: rivals with bigger positions, factories it doesn't own, and government rules. The MI308 charge shows these risks can reach the income statement, not just the risk section. The filing also describes an October 2025 OpenAI agreement, but I didn't confirm how that ties into the customer-concentration risk.

question: Which company invests more in research and development, NVIDIA or AMD?
answer:
NVIDIA spends more on R&D in dollars. In its fiscal year ended January 25, 2026, NVIDIA spent $18,497M on research and development. AMD spent $8,091M in its fiscal year ended December 27, 2025. The two year-ends are about a month apart, so I treated them as the closest match. Measured against revenue, AMD spends a bigger share.

## What the filing says
- **NVIDIA:** R&D was $18,497M in the year ended Jan 25, 2026, up from $12,914M in the year ended Jan 26, 2025 and $8,675M in the year ended Jan 28, 2024 [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51].
- **AMD:** R&D was $8,091M in the year ended Dec 27, 2025, up from $6,456M in 2024 and $5,872M in 2023 [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.74].
- **Gap:** NVIDIA's R&D was about $10.4B higher than AMD's (18,497 − 8,091). That is roughly 2.3 times AMD's figure (18,497 ÷ 8,091).
- **Growth:** NVIDIA's R&D rose about 43% in the latest year (18,497 ÷ 12,914). AMD's rose about 25% (8,091 ÷ 6,456).
- **Share of revenue:** NVIDIA's R&D was about 8.6% of its $215,938M revenue [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.51]. AMD's was about 23.4% of its $34,639M revenue [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.74]. Both percentages are my own calculations (R&D ÷ revenue).

## What this might mean
In absolute dollars, NVIDIA puts far more money into R&D than AMD. NVIDIA's revenue is much larger, though, so R&D takes a smaller slice of it. AMD reinvests a larger portion of each revenue dollar into R&D. These figures show spending only, not how effective it is.

question: How many employees do NVIDIA and AMD each have?
answer:
NVIDIA had about 42,000 employees at the end of its fiscal year 2026 (January 25, 2026). AMD had about 31,000 at the end of its fiscal year 2025 (December 27, 2025). The two fiscal years end about a month apart, so these are the closest year-end figures in the filings.

## What the filing says
- **NVIDIA:** "approximately 42,000 employees in 38 countries" at the end of fiscal 2026. About 31,000 worked in research and development, and 11,000 worked in sales, marketing, operations and administration. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.11]
- NVIDIA says more than 80 percent of its workforce has technical roles and its turnover rate in fiscal 2026 was 3.7 percent. [NVIDIA FY2026 10-K, p.11]
- **NVIDIA a year earlier:** about 36,000 employees at the end of fiscal 2025. That is about 6,000 more by fiscal 2026, or roughly 17% (6,000 ÷ 36,000). [NVIDIA FY2025 10-K, p.11]
- **AMD:** "approximately 31,000 employees in our global workforce" as of December 27, 2025. [AMD FY2025 10-K, p.18]
- **AMD a year earlier:** about 28,000 as of December 28, 2024. That is about 3,000 more, or roughly 11% (3,000 ÷ 28,000). [AMD FY2024 10-K, p.17]

## What this might mean
NVIDIA has about 11,000 more employees than AMD in the periods compared (42,000 vs. 31,000). Both companies added staff over the last year shown, and NVIDIA's headcount grew by a larger percentage. These are rounded "approximately" figures, so the exact differences may vary slightly.
